scenes.heading: Data Lineage
scenes.subheading: Tracing data from source to sink
scenes.narration: Data lineage records how data flows and transforms from its origins to its final outputs, letting you trace any value back to its sources and forward to its consumers.

scenes.heading: What lineage gives you
bullets: Impact analysis before you change a table
Root-cause debugging when a metric looks wrong
scenes.narration: Lineage enables impact analysis, so before altering a table you can see every downstream report that depends on it. It powers root-cause debugging by letting you trace a suspicious metric back through its transformations to the offending source. It builds trust because consumers can see exactly how a figure was derived. And it provides the audit evidence regulators demand for how personal or financial data was processed.

scenes.heading: Table-level vs column-level
scenes.narration: Table-level lineage records which datasets feed which, which is cheap to capture and enough to see broad dependencies. Column-level lineage traces individual fields through each transformation, which gives precise impact analysis and lets you follow a specific piece of personal data everywhere it flows. Column-level detail costs more to compute and store, so many teams start with table-level lineage and add column-level tracing for sensitive or high-value columns.

scenes.heading: How lineage is captured
steps: Build a directed graph of nodes
scenes.narration: Lineage is typically built by parsing SQL statements and job definitions to extract each step's inputs and outputs. Those relationships are assembled into a directed graph where nodes are datasets or columns and edges are transformations. Runtime metadata such as run times, row counts, and job owners enriches the graph. Analysts and tools then query that graph to answer impact and root-cause questions across the whole platform.

scenes.heading: Automatic beats manual
scenes.narration: Lineage should be captured automatically rather than drawn by hand. Automated capture parses your queries and orchestration definitions, so it reflects what the pipeline actually does. Because it is derived from the code, it stays accurate as pipelines evolve, whereas hand-drawn diagrams go stale the moment someone ships a change. Open standards such as OpenLineage make it easier to collect consistent lineage across many tools and stitch it into one graph, which is why automatic capture is the only approach that scales.

scenes.text: Lineage turns your pipeline from a black box into a map, making change safe and incidents fast to diagnose.
scenes.narration: Lineage turns an opaque tangle of pipelines into a navigable map, which makes changes safer to plan and incidents far faster to diagnose, so capture it automatically rather than documenting it by hand.
